title: Structure catalogue
description: Building types. A structure is a contiguous run of same-symbol tiles on a map: it blocks movement, absorbs fire, shelters a garrison, and leaves passable rubble when it falls. Masonry is not armour — how much a round hurts a building is a property of the round, not a penetration roll.

symbol.description: Map legend character. Must not collide with terrain symbols . 1 2 3.

hp_per_tile.description: Structural integrity per tile of footprint: a bigger building is a tougher one.

garrison_slots.description: How many units can fight from inside. 0 = not garrisonable.

per_tile.description: Every tile of this type is its own structure, with its own HP and its own sprite. For linear structures -- walls, fences -- whose runs are of arbitrary length, and where a breach must be a one-tile hole rather than a whole vanished perimeter. Note this makes roe_penalty a per-tile charge. A compact building leaves this false.

roe_penalty.description: ROE cost when the player brings this building down. A shed is nothing; a civic hall is a strategic defeat dressed as a tactical win. Note that a per_tile type is charged per tile.

low_profile.description: Chest-high: blocks movement and shields whoever is hugging it, but sight and fire pass over it. For fences and perimeter walls. A compound built from sight-blocking masonry is a blind box whose garrison cannot shoot out, so the wall ends up protecting the besieger.

standing_cover.description: Cover level for a unit fighting from immediately behind this while it stands -- the companion to rubble_cover, which is what remains once it does not. Only consulted for a low_profile type.

produces_for.description: Which side this structure builds units for. Present ONLY on production structures -- the seven civilian types are neutral terrain and carry no owner at all, because nothing needed one until a camp did. While a living structure of a type with produces_for === side stands, that side's requestBuild deploys beside it; destroying every one of them stops that side's production. Missions with no such structure fall back to the mission's own player_start, which is what keeps every mission authored before this feature working unchanged.
